atoms.text: ThumbForge generates JPEG thumbnails from images that users upload, reading originals from the bucket media-uploads-prod under the prefix incoming/ and writing results to the prefix thumbs/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named thumbforge-processor and set its trust policy to allow the service principal thumbforge.service.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows GetObject on media-uploads-prod/incoming/* and PutObject on media-uploads-prod/thumbs/*. Do not modify the bucket policy of media-uploads-prod, because no statement is needed there for this setup. In the ThumbForge job configuration, set the execution role field to the ARN of thumbforge-processor. When a job starts, the service obtains temporary credentials for the role and signs every read and write request with them. To verify, upload a test image to incoming/ and confirm that a thumbnail object appears under thumbs/, and that a write attempt outside thumbs/ returns AccessDenied.

ThumbForge generates JPEG thumbnails from images that users upload, reading originals from the bucket media-uploads-prod under the prefix incoming/ and writing results to the prefix thumbs/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal. Open the policy editor for media-uploads-prod and add a statement whose Principal is the service principal thumbforge.service.example. In that statement, allow GetObject on media-uploads-prod/incoming/* and PutObject on media-uploads-prod/thumbs/*. Do not create an IAM role or attach any identity-based policy, because the bucket policy is the only place where these permissions are defined. In the ThumbForge job configuration, leave the execution role field empty so the service uses its own identity. When a job starts, the service sends every read and write request as that principal, and the storage service evaluates each request against the bucket policy. To verify, upload a test image to incoming/ and confirm that a thumbnail object appears under thumbs/, and that a write attempt outside thumbs/ returns AccessDenied.

DocLens extracts text from scanned PDF files, reading each source file from the bucket scans-intake under the prefix pdf/ and writing a JSON result with the same base name to the prefix extracted/ in the bucket scans-intake. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named doclens-extractor whose trust policy names the service principal doclens.service.example as the entity allowed to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role with two statements: GetObject on scans-intake/pdf/* and PutObject on scans-intake/extracted/*. Leave the bucket policy of scans-intake unchanged. Enter the ARN of doclens-extractor in the extraction pipeline's role setting. For each pipeline run, the service requests temporary credentials for the role and uses them when it downloads a PDF and uploads the JSON output. Set the role's maximum session duration to at least the longest expected run, such as two hours for files over 500 pages. After a test run, check that extracted/ contains one JSON object per processed PDF and that the role has no permission to delete objects in pdf/.

DocLens extracts text from scanned PDF files, reading each source file from the bucket scans-intake under the prefix pdf/ and writing a JSON result with the same base name to the prefix extracted/ in the bucket scans-intake. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal. Add a statement to the bucket policy of scans-intake whose Principal is the service principal doclens.service.example. Give that statement two permissions: GetObject on scans-intake/pdf/* and PutObject on scans-intake/extracted/*. Do not create an IAM role for this setup, since the bucket policy carries all permissions. Leave the role setting of the extraction pipeline blank so the service calls the storage service under its own identity. For each pipeline run, the service downloads a PDF and uploads the JSON output as that principal, and every request is authorized by the bucket policy. Because no role session is involved, there is no session duration to configure, and long runs over 500 pages are not interrupted by credential expiry. After a test run, check that extracted/ contains one JSON object per processed PDF and that the bucket policy grants no permission to delete objects in pdf/.

ReelPress transcodes raw MP4 recordings into HLS segments, reading source videos from the bucket studio-raw under the prefix camera/ and writing playlists and segment files to the bucket studio-delivery under the prefix hls/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named reelpress-transcoder and configure its trust policy so that the service principal reelpress.service.example can assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows GetObject on studio-raw/camera/* and PutObject plus AbortMultipartUpload on studio-delivery/hls/*. Do not edit the bucket policies of studio-raw or studio-delivery. Register the role ARN in the transcoding profile under the field named execution role. At the start of each job, the service assumes the role and uses the resulting temporary credentials for reading the source and uploading each segment. Multipart uploads are used for segments larger than 100 MB, which is why the abort permission is included. Confirm the setup by submitting a short clip and checking that an index.m3u8 playlist appears under hls/.

ReelPress transcodes raw MP4 recordings into HLS segments, reading source videos from the bucket studio-raw under the prefix camera/ and writing playlists and segment files to the bucket studio-delivery under the prefix hls/. Access is granted only through the resource-based policies of the two buckets, which name the service principal. Add a statement to the policy of studio-raw with the Principal reelpress.service.example that allows GetObject on studio-raw/camera/*. Add a statement to the policy of studio-delivery with the same Principal that allows PutObject plus AbortMultipartUpload on studio-delivery/hls/*. Do not create any IAM role for this service. Leave the execution role field of the transcoding profile empty so the service acts under its own identity. At the start of each job, the service reads the source and uploads each segment as that principal, and each bucket policy authorizes its own requests. Multipart uploads are used for segments larger than 100 MB, which is why the abort permission is included. Confirm the setup by submitting a short clip and checking that an index.m3u8 playlist appears under hls/.

VoxScribe converts recorded audio into text transcripts, reading WAV and FLAC files from the bucket call-recordings under the prefix audio/ and writing transcript files in WebVTT format to the prefix transcripts/ of the same bucket. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named voxscribe-worker and set its trust policy to permit the service principal voxscribe.service.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows GetObject on call-recordings/audio/* and PutObject on call-recordings/transcripts/*, and also ListBucket on call-recordings restricted to those two prefixes by a condition. The bucket policy of call-recordings is left as it is. In the transcription settings, supply the role ARN in the field labeled service role. Each batch causes the service to assume the role, enumerate new files in audio/, and write one transcript per recording using the temporary credentials. To test, place a 30-second FLAC file in audio/ and verify that a .vtt object with the same base name appears in transcripts/.

VoxScribe converts recorded audio into text transcripts, reading WAV and FLAC files from the bucket call-recordings under the prefix audio/ and writing transcript files in WebVTT format to the prefix transcripts/ of the same bucket. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal. Add a statement to the bucket policy of call-recordings with the Principal voxscribe.service.example. In it, allow GetObject on call-recordings/audio/* and PutObject on call-recordings/transcripts/*, and also ListBucket on call-recordings restricted to those two prefixes by a condition. No IAM role is created, and nothing is attached to any identity. In the transcription settings, leave the service role field empty so the service uses its own identity. Each batch causes the service to enumerate new files in audio/ and write one transcript per recording as that principal, with each request checked against the bucket policy. To test, place a 30-second FLAC file in audio/ and verify that a .vtt object with the same base name appears in transcripts/.

PageShift converts word-processor documents to PDF, reading DOCX files from the bucket contracts-drafts under the prefix submitted/ and writing the converted PDF to the prefix converted/ in the bucket contracts-archive. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role called pageshift-converter and edit its trust policy so that the service principal pageshift.service.example is the trusted entity. Attach an identity-based policy that grants GetObject on contracts-drafts/submitted/* and PutObject on contracts-archive/converted/*. Do not change the bucket policy of either bucket. Put the role ARN into the conversion queue configuration under the property named assume role. For every queued document, the service assumes the role, downloads the DOCX file, renders it, and uploads the PDF using temporary credentials. The output key keeps the original base name and replaces the extension with .pdf. Validate the setup by queueing one DOCX file and confirming that a PDF of the same base name exists under converted/.

PageShift converts word-processor documents to PDF, reading DOCX files from the bucket contracts-drafts under the prefix submitted/ and writing the converted PDF to the prefix converted/ in the bucket contracts-archive. Access is granted only through the resource-based policies of the two buckets, which name the service principal. Add a statement to the policy of contracts-drafts that names pageshift.service.example as Principal and grants GetObject on contracts-drafts/submitted/*. Add a statement to the policy of contracts-archive that names the same Principal and grants PutObject on contracts-archive/converted/*. Do not create an IAM role for this service. Leave the assume role property in the conversion queue configuration unset. For every queued document, the service downloads the DOCX file, renders it, and uploads the PDF under its own service identity. The output key keeps the original base name and replaces the extension with .pdf. Validate the setup by queueing one DOCX file and confirming that a PDF of the same base name exists under converted/.

MarkStamp applies visible watermarks to product photos, reading originals from the bucket catalog-photos under the prefix originals/ and writing watermarked JPEG files to the prefix public/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named markstamp-runner with a trust policy naming the service principal markstamp.service.example. Attach an identity-based policy that allows GetObject on catalog-photos/originals/* and PutObject on catalog-photos/public/*. Do not add or edit anystatement in the bucket policy of catalog-photos, including the existing public-read statement for public/. In the MarkStamp project settings, select the role by its ARN. When a watermark job runs, the service uses temporary credentials from the role to fetch each original and to write the stamped copy. Originals are never overwritten because the role has no write permission on originals/. Test by submitting one photo and confirming that its watermarked copy is present under public/ while originals/ is unchanged.

MarkStamp applies visible watermarks to product photos, reading originals from the bucket catalog-photos under the prefix originals/ and writing watermarked JPEG files to the prefix public/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal. Add a statement to the bucket policy of catalog-photos with the Principal markstamp.service.example. In that statement, allow GetObject on catalog-photos/originals/* and PutObject on catalog-photos/public/*, and leave the existing public-read statement for public/ as it is. Do not create an IAM role for this service. In the MarkStamp project settings, leave the role selection empty so the service uses its own identity. When a watermark job runs, the service fetches each original and writes the stamped copy as that principal. Originals are never overwritten because the statement grants no write permission on originals/. Test by submitting one photo and confirming that its watermarked copy is present under public/ while originals/ is unchanged.

InvoiceReader performs optical character recognition on invoice images, reading TIFF and PNG files from the bucket finance-inbox under the prefix invoices/ and writing a CSV of recognized fields to the prefix parsed/ in the bucket finance-ledger-staging. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named invoicereader-ocr and set its trust policy to allow the service principal invoicereader.service.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows GetObject on finance-inbox/invoices/* and PutObject on finance-ledger-staging/parsed/*. Neither bucket policy is modified. Enter the role ARN in the recognition job template. Each job begins with the service assuming the role, after which it reads the images and uploads one CSV per invoice batch with the temporary credentials. CSV files are named with the batch ID and a UTC timestamp. Verify by running a batch of five images and checking that a single CSV appears under parsed/ and that listing finance-inbox outside invoices/ is denied.

InvoiceReader performs optical character recognition on invoice images, reading TIFF and PNG files from the bucket finance-inbox under the prefix invoices/ and writing a CSV of recognized fields to the prefix parsed/ in the bucket finance-ledger-staging. Access is granted only through the resource-based policies of the two buckets, which name the service principal. In the policy of finance-inbox, add a statement for the Principal invoicereader.service.example that allows GetObject on finance-inbox/invoices/*. In the policy of finance-ledger-staging, add a statement for the same Principal that allows PutObject on finance-ledger-staging/parsed/*. No IAM role is created for this service. Leave the role field in the recognition job template empty. Each job begins with the service reading the images and uploading one CSV per invoice batch under its own service identity. CSV files are named with the batch ID and a UTC timestamp. Verify by running a batch of five images and checking that a single CSV appears under parsed/ and that listing finance-inbox outside invoices/ is denied.

ArchivePack bundles processed media files into ZIP archives, reading files from the bucket project-assets under the prefix final/ and writing one ZIP per project to the prefix bundles/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the service assumes. Create a role named archivepack-bundler and write its trust policy so that the service principal archivepack.service.example may assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows GetObject on project-assets/final/*, ListBucket on project-assets limited to the final/ prefix, and PutObject on project-assets/bundles/*. Do not touch the bucket policy of project-assets. Specify the role ARN in the bundling task definition. A task starts with the service assuming the role, then listing the project's files, streaming them into a ZIP, and uploading the archive using temporary credentials. Archive keys follow the pattern bundles/PROJECT_ID.zip. Check the setup by bundling a project with ten files and confirming that the ZIP object exists and lists all ten entries.

ArchivePack bundles processed media files into ZIP archives, reading files from the bucket project-assets under the prefix final/ and writing one ZIP per project to the prefix bundles/ in the same bucket. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal. Add a statement to the bucket policy of project-assets with the Principal archivepack.service.example. In that statement, allow GetObject on project-assets/final/*, ListBucket on project-assets limited to the final/ prefix, and PutObject on project-assets/bundles/*. Do not create an IAM role for this service. Leave the role field in the bundling task definition empty. A task starts with the service listing the project's files, streaming them into a ZIP, and uploading the archive as that principal. Archive keys follow the pattern bundles/PROJECT_ID.zip. Check the setup by bundling a project with ten files and confirming that the ZIP object exists and lists all ten entries.
